key_insight: An ensemble-consensus semi-supervised objective improves molecular graph prediction by using unlabeled data without needing label-preserving augmentations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to more accurate and better-calibrated property predictors for drug discovery and materials screening, especially when labels are scarce but unlabeled molecules are abundant.
method: Train graph neural networks with an ensemble consensus loss on labeled and unlabeled molecular graphs.
Use agreement among ensemble members as the learning signal instead of hand-designed molecular augmentations.
Leverage the consensus objective to increase robustness and reduce calibration error, with single members sometimes surpassing traditional supervised ensembles.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains across a diverse range of molecular datasets, task types, and GNN architectures, including improved accuracy and calibration.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on reliable ensemble diversity and careful tuning of the consensus objective, so implementation overhead and stability should be checked.
paper_title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus
